title: Mapping Disorder and Electronic Structure in Amorphous Bi2O3 using 4D-STEM and Spectroscopy
content: Amorphization in α-Bi2O3 under ion irradiation is a complex process with significant implications for its structural stability and functional properties. This study investigates the effects of He, Ne, and Ar irradiation on Bi2O3 using advanced electron microscopy techniques to analyze defect accumulation, mass transport, and changes in electronic structure. Unlike many crystalline materials, where amorphization initiates at the depth of maximum damage, Bi2O3 amorphizes from the surface downward (Fig. 1), suggesting an intricate disordering mechanism governed by both nuclear and electronic stopping [1]. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy (TEM) reveals the progressive loss of crystallinity, while electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) provides insight into changes in the local bonding environment and electronic structure. The formation and evolution of gas bubbles within the irradiated matrix serve as direct evidence of enhanced mass transport, with oxygen vacancy mobility and Bi diffusion playing key roles in the coarsening process [2,3].
